How an hourly wage becomes a salary

Every guide in this directory starts with the same standard schedule: 40 hours a week for 52 paid weeks — 2,080 work hours a year. Multiply any hourly rate by 2,080 and you have its annual salary equivalent: $20 an hour is $41,600 a year, and $30 an hour is $62,400. Weekly pay is the rate times your hours, and monthly pay is the annual figure divided by 12.

Your own schedule changes the answer. At 30 hours a week, that same $20 rate pays $31,200 a year instead of $41,600, because the year holds 1,560 scheduled hours rather than 2,080. Unpaid weeks reduce the total further, while overtime hours add premium pay on top — each guide shows the standard total first, then explains how part-time hours, unpaid time and overtime move it. Our guide to how many hours a week count as full-time explains why the 40-hour baseline is a convention rather than a legal definition.

All figures are gross pay, before taxes and other deductions. To run your own rate against your own schedule — any hours, any weeks — use the hourly to salary calculator, and for hours beyond 40 in a week, the overtime calculator prices the premium separately.

Common questions

How do I convert an hourly wage to a yearly salary?

Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours and your paid weeks. On the standard schedule — 40 hours a week for 52 weeks — that is simply your rate times 2,080 hours: $25 an hour becomes $52,000 a year.

How many work hours are there in a year?

A full-time schedule of 40 hours a week adds up to 2,080 hours in a 52-week year. Part-time schedules total less — 30 hours a week is 1,560 hours — and holidays and unpaid leave reduce the hours actually worked.

Are these annual figures before or after tax?

Before tax. Every figure in these guides is gross pay, calculated before income tax, Social Security and Medicare, and any benefit deductions. Your take-home pay will be lower; our gross pay vs net pay guide explains where the difference goes.
